headline: Pressure behavior is specified but NOT executable in the current core deploy.

problem.summary: Six AGENTS.md-mandated adversarial tests target PPA methods (delegate, dispute_payment, issue_invoice and getters) that were gas-modularized out of the core to fit the Bradbury per-tx ceiling.
problem.previousState: 6 failed, 150 passed, 2 skipped — the repository's reported test state contained six unresolved adversarial questions.
problem.notRegressions: Caused by the earlier modularization, not by the v0.3 origin work or the vector-runner hardening.
problem.whyNotJustLeaveThem: Six red tests misreport repository state. Deleting or migrating them would destroy the specification of the negative properties.

resolution.action: Each test marked skipped via @modularized_out('<extension>') with an explicit reason.
resolution.assertionsPreserved: verbatim; no assertion deleted, weakened, or rewritten
resolution.skipIsNotAPass: Every skip reason ends with 'This skip is not a pass.'
resolution.mandatoryPropertyCarried: Every skip reason states the property that remains mandatory when the extension returns.

classified.mandatory: delegation narrows limits and never widens; revocation kills future spend immediately
an expired delegation confers no authority
the account allowlist still binds a delegate
refund is a compensating entry; settled history is never rewritten; no double refund
dispute requires an existing payment and correct authority; duplicate disputes rejected
an invoice settles exactly once and only through the send gates

guardCovers: every skip is classified against a known extension and retains its assertions (assert or pytest.raises)
skipped tests only touch methods that are genuinely modularized out
no UNSKIPPED test calls a method that exists in no primitive implementation (drift guard)
every skip reason carries the classification, the mandatory property, and 'not a pass'
the public-method union is non-trivial, so the drift guard cannot be vacuous
tests.guardMutationProved: Removing one skip marker makes three tests fail: the unskipped test itself plus both classification guards. The guard is not decorative.

adversarialQuestionsStillUnexecutable: Can delegation widen account authority? (delegation extension absent)
Does an expired delegation lose authority? (delegation extension absent)
Does the account allowlist bind a delegate? (delegation extension absent)
Is a refund compensating rather than a rewrite, and single-shot? (dispute/refund extension absent)
Are dispute lookups and authority guarded? (dispute/refund extension absent)
Does an invoice settle exactly once through send gates? (invoice extension absent)

suiteAccounting.delta: 6 failed -> 6 skipped; 5 new guard tests added (150 -> 155 passed)
suiteAccounting.meaning: The repository no longer reports a red suite, and the six adversarial questions are explicitly classified rather than silently absent.

retainedAuthorityValues.note: Recorded separately and unchanged by this work. The authority fingerprint covers specification documents; the implementation hash covers source bytes. They are distinct identities and are never combined.

notDone: delegate / invoice / dispute methods were NOT restored to the core
the superseded v0.2 spine vectors were NOT migrated
no primitive implementation, CAPABILITY.json, or capability version was touched
next: WORK-PPA-SPLIT: split PPA Core (ledger, policy/attestation, capital, send gates, settlement) from the Receipt/Proposal Adapter (adjudicator registry, origin binding, authority fingerprint, receipt validation, replay protection, proposal state). The adapter must be the only authorized proposal caller into Core. The adjudication producer remains a third contract and stays blocked until an origin-bound adapter is deployed.
